scope: Offline synthetic fixtures on the workspace HDD; no ETL, assets, production output or checkpoints changed.
baseline: Workspace infra/parquet_sort.py copied before this task, including preexisting external sort/staging changes; helper invoked without the unsupported producer batch_size argument.

fixture.generator: numpy.default_rng(721), ten chunks of 100000 rows. For each chunk, draw uint8[100000,16], hex encode each row into 32 characters; next draw empresa_id and id as uniform UInt64 arrays in [0, 2**64). Sixteen text columns contain identical copies of that chunk text vector. ParquetWriter default Snappy, row_group_size=65536.
fixture.small: Four 250000-row LazyFrame slices of the base file, one million rows total.
fixture.large: Eight LazyFrame scans of the base file, eight million rows total, each complete row repeated eight times.

limitations: Single observations per configuration, run sequentially with OS cache enabled, without cache eviction or explicit fsync; cache, writeback and other workloads affect timings. This is not a controlled cold-disk benchmark or a forecast for the full dataset.
RSS sampled at 50 ms and summed over the helper process and living descendants. Shared pages may be counted twice; includes imports and allocator-retained pages, not just active sort memory.

All column values were compared exactly between the one-million-row outputs. For eight million rows, compared all sort-key pairs exactly, including their eightfold multiplicity, plus schemas, row counts and global physical order. Large payload columns were not compared in that audit.
Range redistribution costs more staging work and creates more files. The one-million-row fixture regressed with the default 256 MiB pool. Only the establishments producer opts into this strategy.
Only the published establishments footer was read (72605022 rows); production inputs and the full ETL were not executed.
